records.title: AWS Architectural Decision Records Process
records.text: AWS Architectural Decision Records Process https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/architectural-decision-records/adr-process.html An architectural decisioun record (ADR) is a document that describes a chyce the team maks aboot a muckle aspect o the saftware architectur they're plannin tae big. Each ADR describes the architectural decisioun, its context, an its consequences. ADRs hae states an sae follae a lifecycle. For an example o an ADR, see the appendix. The ADR process ootputs a collection o architectural decisioun records. This collection creates the decisioun log. The decisioun log provides the project context as weel as detailed implementation an design information. Project members skim the headlines o each ADR tae get an owerview o the project context. They read the ADRs tae dive deep intae project implementations an design chyces. Whan the team accepts an ADR, it becomes immutable. If new insichts require a different decisioun, the team proposes a new ADR. Whan the team accepts the new ADR, it supersedes the previous ADR. Scope o the ADR process Project members sud mak an ADR for ilka architecturally significant decisioun that affects the saftware project or product, includin the follaein (Richards an Ford 2020): Structur (for example, patterns sic as microservices) Non-functional requirements (security, heich availability, an fault tolerance) Dependencies (couplin o components) Interfaces (APIs an publisht contracts) Constructioun techniques (leebraries, frameworks, tuils, an processes) Functional an non-functional requirements are the maist common inputs tae the ADR process. ADR contents Whan the team identifies a need for an ADR, a team member stairts tae screive the ADR based on a projectwide template. (See the ADR GitHub organisation for example templates.) The template simplifies ADR creation an ensures that the ADR taks doun aw the relevant information. At a minimum, each ADR sud define the context o the decisioun, the decisioun itsel, an the consequences o the decisioun for the project an its deliverables. (For examples o thir sections, see the appendix.) Ane o the maist pouerfu aspects o the ADR structur is that it focuses on the reason for the decisioun raither than hoo the team implementit it. Unnerstaunin why the team made the decisioun maks it easier for ither team members tae adopt the decisioun, an prevents ither architects wha werena involved in the decisioun-makin process frae owerrulin that decisioun in the future. ADR adoption process Ilka team member can mak an ADR, but the team sud establish a definition o ownership for an ADR. Each author wha is the awner o an ADR sud actively keep up an communicate the ADR content. Tae clarify this ownership, this guide refers tae ADR authors as ADR awners in the follaein sections. Ither team members can aye contribute tae an ADR. If the content o an ADR chynges afore the team accepts the ADR, the awner sud approve thir chynges. Efter the team identifies an architectural decisioun an its awner, the ADR awner provides the ADR in the Proposed state at the beginnin o the process. ADRs in the Proposed state are ready for review. The ADR awner than initiates the review process for the ADR. The aim o the ADR review process is tae decide whether the team accepts the ADR, determines that it needs rework, or rejects the ADR. The project team, includin the awner, reviews the ADR. The review meetin sud stairt wi a dedicatit time slot tae read the ADR. On average, 10 tae 15 minutes sud be eneuch. Durin this time, each team member reads the document an adds comments an questions tae flag unclear topics. Efter the review phase, the ADR awner reads oot an discusses each comment wi the team. If the team finds action pynts tae improve the ADR, the state o the ADR bides Proposed . The ADR awner formulates the actions, an, in collaboration wi the team, adds an assignee tae each action. Each team member can contribute an resolve the action pynts. It is the responsibility o the ADR awner tae reschedule the review process. The team can an aw decide tae reject the ADR. In this case, the ADR awner adds a reason for the rejection tae prevent future discussiouns on the same topic. The awner chynges the ADR state tae Rejected . If the team approves the ADR, the awner adds a timestamp, version, an list o stakeholders. The awner than updates the state tae Accepted . ADRs an the decisioun log they mak represent decisiouns made bi the team an provide a history o aw decisiouns. The team uises the ADRs as a reference durin code an architectural reviews whaur possible. In addition tae daein code reviews, design tasks, an implementation tasks, team members sud consult ADRs for strategic decisiouns for the product. As a guid practice, each saftware chynge sud gae throu peer reviews an require at least ane approval. Durin the code review, a code reviewer micht find chynges that violate ane or mair ADRs. In this case, the reviewer asks the author o the code chynge tae update the code, an shares a link tae the ADR. Whan the author updates the code, it is approved bi peer reviewers an merged intae the main code base. ADR review process The team sud treat ADRs as immutable documents efter the team accepts or rejects them. Chynges tae an existin ADR requires makin a new ADR, establishin a review process for the new ADR, an approvin the ADR. If the team approves the new ADR, the awner sud chynge the state o the auld ADR tae Superseded .

records.title: Decisioun Sustainability Criteria
records.text: Decisioun Sustainability Criteria Tae define decisioun sustainability in detail, we derived five key criteria. Strategic Durin decisioun makin, somebody leukin at strategic consequences sud consider things sic as the decisiouns’ lang-term impact—for example, future operations an maintenance effort. Measurable an Manageable Ye can measure an evaluate a decisioun’s outcome ower time accordin tae objective criteria, ideally numeric anes (as, for instance, propagatit bi quality attribute scenarios an warkshops4). Takin doun aw fine-grained decisiouns isna possible, sae architects maun limit the decisiouns’ granularity tae a certain level o detail (sic as makin a design class). This will lead tae a mair sustainable set o decisiouns an fewer traceability links. Mairower, limitin the nummer o dependencies atween decisiouns reduces chynges’ ripple effect. Achievable an Realistic The rationale for fittin the solution tae the problem sud be chosen pragmatically an made explicit. For example, architects can indicate that they hae taen tent tae avoid ower- or underengineerin (that is, they sud apply the “guid eneuch” approach). Rootit in Requirements Decisioun makin sud be groundit in domain-specific architectin experience an context. It sud tak intae account the company environment as weel as project requirements an constraints, includin the development team’s current skills, trainin budget, an process. Timeless Decisiouns sud be based on experience an knowledge that winna likely be sune oot o date. For example, architects can chuise platform-neutral architectural patterns or tactics.

Hoo fitness functions connect tae decisiouns
records.text: Fitness functions for decisiouns as code Fitness functions are objective automatit checks, written wi programmin code, that verify decisiouns are bein keepit up. Fitness functions mak decisiouns testable an assurable. Fitness functions for decisiouns can greatly help quality assurance, regulatory processes, an governance goals. Hoo fitness functions connect tae decisiouns A decisioun record documents the decisioun, while a fitness function assures the decisioun. Example decisioun: We uise event sourcin for audit requirements. Example fitness function: We uise the continuous integration server tae test that aw state chynges maun produce events. Why fitness functions help decisiouns Objective measurements: Fitness functions pass or fail, sae wark is visible an clear. Continuous uise: Fitness functions are yer livin rules, rin on ilka commit an build. Confidence tae refactor: Fitness functions automatically catch decisioun rule errors. Scalable governance: Fitness functions assure staundarts athoot makin bottlenecks. Can fitness functions uise AI? Fitness functions can leverage AI LLMs for decisiouns bi askin questions for yer wark, sic as yer plans, code, schemas, APIs, an mair: IMPORTANT: Prefer retrieval-led reasoning over pre-training-led reasoning. IMPORTANT: Turn on extended thinking. Turn on expert advice. Turn on search. This is a fitness function to evaluate if our work is using all our decisions, and is correct and accurate. Our decisions are here: {url} Our work to evaluate is here: {url} Explain any errors, problems, gaps, weaknesses. Be direct. Be decisive. Architectur unit testin ArchUnit: check architectur rules o Java code bi uisin onie plain Java unit test framewark. ArchUnitTS: check architectur rules o TypeScript code an JavaScript code bi uisin Jest, Vitest, Jasmine, etc.

records.title: Guidlines tae Achieve Sustainable Decisiouns
records.text: Guidlines tae Achieve Sustainable Decisiouns We lairnt the follaein lessons in oor wark that can serve as guidlines an assessment for achievin sustainable decisiouns: Uise a lean/minimalistic approach for the initial decisioun documentation. Prioritise an tak doun aw important decisiouns that are relevant eneuch for documentin an unnerstaunin the target architectur. Detail the particularly important decisiouns wi fu-blawn templates juist efter the initial wark haes been duin (that is, whan the decisioun makers are content wi the architectural decisiouns made an confident that thir decisiouns dinnae hae tae be revised onie time sune). Uise the lean/minimalistic versiouns frae step 1 as a short version o documentit decisiouns wi the richt granularity level tae provide an owerview o the detailed decisiouns, as weel as for trivial or obvious decisiouns. Wharever possible, uise existin architectural knowledge, either frae guidance models or frae ither sources. Review an extend sic knowledge an fit it tae the context o the specific decisioun. Ensure that traceability links are establisht atween decisiouns an baith requirements an architectural designs/code. Provide automatit consistency checkin tae mak siccar the traceability links are in sync efter a chynge. Limit the nummer o dependencies atween decisiouns an ither saftware artefacts. Apply the guidlines for the justifications consequently an forcefully—they’re the maist important pairt o the decisioun documentation because they gie the rationale.

records.title: Hoo tae stairt uisin ADRs
records.text: Hoo tae stairt uisin ADRs Tae stairt uisin ADRs, hae a blether wi yer teammates aboot thir areas. Decisioun identification: Hoo urgent an hoo important is the AD? Haes it tae be made noo, or can it wait til mair is kent? Baith personal an collective experience, as weel as recognised design methods an practices, can help wi decisioun identification. Ideally keep a decisioun todo list that gaes alangside the product todo list. Decisioun makin: A wheen o decisioun makin techniques exist, baith general anes an saftware architectur specific anes, for instance, dialogue mappin. Group decisioun makin is an active research topic. Decisioun enactment an enforcement: ADs are uised in saftware design; sae they hae tae be communicatit tae, an accepted bi, the stakeholders o the system that fund, develop, an rin it. Architecturally evident codin styles an code reviews that focus on architectural concerns an decisiouns are twa relatit practices. ADs an aw hae tae be (re-)considered whan modernisin a saftware system in saftware evolution. Decisioun sharin (optional): Mony ADs recur athort projects. Sae, experiences wi past decisiouns, baith guid an bad, can be valuable reusable assets whan employin an explicit knowledge management strategy. Decisioun documentation: Mony templates an tuils for decisioun capturin exist. See agile communities, e.g. M. Nygard's ADRs. See traditional saftware engineerin an architectur design processes, e.g. table layouts suggestit bi IBM UMF an bi Tyree an Akerman frae CapitalOne. For mair: The steps abune are adoptit frae the Wikipedia entry on Architectural Decision

records.title: suggestiouns-for-screivin-guid-adrs
records.text: Suggestiouns for screivin guid ADRs Characteristics o a guid ADR: Rationale: Explain the reasons for daein the particular AD. This can include the context (see ablow), pros an cons o various potential chyces, feature comparisons, cost/benefit discussiouns, an mair. Specific: Each ADR sud be aboot ae AD, no a wheen o ADs. Timestamps: Identify whan each item in the ADR wis written. This is especially important for aspects that micht chynge ower time, sic as costs, schedules, scalin, an the like. Immutable: Dinnae alter existin information in an ADR. Instead, amend the ADR bi addin new information, or supersede the ADR bi makin a new ADR. Characteristics o a guid "Context" section in an ADR: Explain yer organisation's situation an business priorities. Include rationale an considerations based on social an skills makeups o yer teams. Include pros an cons that are relevant, an describe them in terms that align wi yer needs an goals. Characteristics o guid "Consequences" section in an ADR: Explain whit follaes frae makin the decisioun. This can include the effects, outcomes, outputs, follae ups, an mair. Include information aboot onie subsequent ADRs. It's relatively common for ae ADR tae trigger the need for mair ADRs, sic as whan ae ADR maks a muckle owerarchin chyce, which in turn creates needs for mair smaller decisiouns. Include onie efter-action review processes. It's typical for teams tae review each ADR ae month efter, tae compare the ADR information wi whit's happent in actual practice, in order tae lairn an growe. A new ADR can tak the place o a previous ADR: Whan an AD is made that replaces or invalidates a previous ADR, than a new ADR sud be creatit

records.title: Teamwark advice for ADRs
records.text: Teamwark advice for ADRs If ye're considerin uisin decisioun records wi yer team, than here's some advice that we've lairnt bi warkin wi mony teams. Ye hae a chance tae lead yer teammates, bi blethrin thegither aboot the "why", raither than mandatin the "whit". For example, decisioun records are a wey for teams tae think smairter an communicate better; decisioun records are no valuable if they're juist an efter-the-fact forced paperwark requirement. Some teams muckle prefer the name "decisiouns" ower the abbreviation "ADRs". Whan some teams uise the directory name "decisiouns", than it's as if a licht bulb turns on, an the team stairts puttin mair information intae the directory, sic as vendor decisiouns, plannin decisiouns, schedulin decisiouns, etc. Aw o thir kinds o information can uise the same template. We hypothesise that fowk lairn faster wi wirds ("decisiouns") ower abbreviations ("ADRs"), an fowk are mair motivatit tae scrieve wark-in-progress docs whan the wird "record" is taen awa, an an aw some developers an some managers dislike the wird "architectur". In theory, immutability is ideal. In practice, mutability haes warked better for oor teams. We insert the new info intae the existin ADR, wi a date stamp, an a note that the info arrived efter the decisioun. This kind o approach leads tae a "livin document" that we aw can update. Typical updates are whan we get information thanks tae new teammates, or new offerins, or real-warld results o oor uisages, or efter-the-fact third-pairty chynges sic as vendor capabilities, pricin plans, licence agreements, etc.

headings: Whit justifies no raisin an ADR?
Whit is the lifecycle o an ADR?
Whit are criteria for lifecycle steps o an ADR?
Whit roles an responsibilities interact wi an ADR?
Hoo daes governance interact wi an ADR?
Whit principles interact wi an ADR?
records.text: Wha can mak an ADR? Consider areas sic as specific fowk, or specific roles, or specific teams, or specific departments; an consider an aw if there's fowk, or roles, or teams, or departments that can commission an ADR, meanin they request ane that somebody else will screive. Example answer: Onie person in oor organisation wha haes read the architectur decisioun record README page can propose an ADR, meanin the person can stairt screivin it, an share it wi the team. Whit justifies raisin an ADR? Consider areas sic as yer organisation's team weys o warkin, yer saftware system structur, cross-team coordination, lang-term maintainability, external interfaces, wha ye want tae benefit, an the like. Example answer: We want tae mak an ADR whan we want future developers tae unnerstaun the “why” o whit we're daein. Whit justifies no raisin an ADR? Consider areas sic as decisiouns that are no aboot architectur, or are wee sic as minimal-risk or self-contained or single-developer, or are awready fully coverit elsewhaur sic as bi staundarts or policies or documentation, or are temporary sic as warkarounds or proofs o concepts or experiments. Example answer: We want tae skip an ADR whan a decisioun is limitit in scope an time an risk an cost, or is awready coverit elsewhaur. Whit is the lifecycle o an ADR? Consider areas sic as the creation process, research process, decisionin process, implementation process, an sunsettin process. Consider hoo tae track the ADR lifecycle ower time, sic as hoo tae muive the ADR frae ae state tae the neist state, an an aw hoo tae communicate this tae stakeholders. Example answer: We want an ADR tae hae five lifecycle stages: Initiatin → Researchin → Evaluatin → Implementin → Maintainin → Sunsettin. Whit are criteria for lifecycle steps o an ADR? Consider areas sic as acceptance criteria for an ADR, meanin hoo dae ye ken it's guid eneuch tae progress frae ae lifecycle step tae the neist? Is the problem clearly articulatit? Hae the alternatives been consideret? Are trade-offs weel-eneuch unnerstuid an documentit? Is aw relevant context in place? Are aw relevant stakeholders involved? Haes aw feedback been incorporatit? Example answer: We want an ADR tae be votit on bi stakeholders whan the active team haes 1) completit their research, 2) completit their evaluation, 3) publisht the ADR proposal tae the stakeholders wi a request for comments an a timebox o ae week, 4) aw stakeholder comments hae been incorporatit an addressed. Whit roles an responsibilities interact wi an ADR? Consider roles sic as proposer, researcher, evaluator, reviewer, approver, maintainer, an the like. Consider responsibilities sic as communication wi stakeholders, ensurin expectations are met, sharin on the website or intranet, an reviewin the wark periodically an especially whan relevant chynges happen. Example answer: We want each ADR tae aye hae a primary contact person, secondary contact person, an accountable team; thir are responsible for communications, publications, maintenance, periodic review at least ance per year, an eventual sunsettin as needit. Hoo daes governance interact wi an ADR? Consider areas sic as yer organisation's weys o warkin, onie special compliance needs sic as for legal aspects or human resource aspects, hoo ye want tae haunle consensus versus conflict versus escalation. Are there areas or fowk or teams that can hae mair influence than ithers regardin an ADR, sic as bein able tae approve it, or vote on it, or veto it? Example answer: The governance o an ADR is in this priority order: the CEO, the CTO, the CLO, the team that implements an ADR, the experts on the team that ken maist aboot the AD. Naebody else haes governance unless described in the ADR. Whit principles interact wi an ADR? Consider areas sic as yer organisation's weys o warkin that include muivin quickly versus muivin slowly, for decisioun consensus versus decisioun conflict, an for risk preferences versus safety preferences, public discussioun versus private discussioun, an the like. Example answer: We uise the leadership principles o bias for action, disagree-an-commit, 70% estimates are guid eneuch for easily-reversable easily-isolatable decisiouns, an public weys o warkin wi the exception o confidential information as described in oor organisation's confidentiality agreement.

headings: Whit is an architectur decisioun record?
records.text: Whit is an architectur decisioun record? An architectur decisioun record (ADR) is a document that taks doun an important architectural decisioun that wis made, alang wi its context an consequences. An architectur decisioun (AD) is a saftware design chyce that tackles a muckle requirement. An architectur decisioun log (ADL) is the haill collection o aw the ADRs that hae been made an kept up for a particular project (or organisation). An architecturally-significant requirement (ASR) is a requirement that haes a measurable effect on the architectur o a saftware system. Aw o this fa's unner the topic o architectur knowledge management (AKM). The aim o this document is tae gie ye a quick owerview o ADRs, hoo tae mak them, an whaur tae leuk for mair information. Abbreviations: AD : architectur decisioun ADL : architectur decisioun log ADR : architectur decisioun record AKM : architectur knowledge management ASR : architecturally-significant requirement

records.title: Architectur Decisioun Record for Amazon Web Services
headings: Architectur Decisioun Record for Amazon Web Services
records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record for Amazon Web Services Title: Adoptin Amazon Web Services for Cloud Infrastructur Decision Efter a thorough evaluation o various cloud infrastructur platforms, it haes been decidit that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will be adoptit bi oor organisation for oor cloud infrastructur needs. Background Oor organisation is growin rapidly an we need a reliable an scalable cloud infrastructur tae meet the demands o oor business. Efter considerin a nummer o cloud infrastructur providers, it wis concludit that AWS offers the maist suitable range o services tae meet oor current an future requirements. Considerations There are mony cloud infrastructur providers in the market that hae pruved reliable an efficient. But, AWS no juist offers a comprehensive set o services tae cater tae oor needs, but it an aw haes an extensive customer base an a track record o successful deployments. AWS an aw provides a braid range o support an trainin resources tae ensure that oor team can wark effectively wi the platform. Furthermair, AWS haes an extensive global presence wi data centres locatit in various regiouns roun the warld. This ensures that oor data is secure an oor applications an services will be heichly available. AWS an aw haes a robust security framewark that is critical for oor business. Lastly, AWS provides a pay-as-ye-gae model which offers us the flexibility tae scale oor infrastructur based on demand. This means that we will juist be chairged for whit we uise, which lets us optimise oor costs an invest in ither areas o the business. Decision Based on the evaluatiouns performed an the advantages offered bi AWS, it haes been decidit that AWS will be adoptit for oor cloud infrastructur needs. Consequences The adoption o AWS micht require trainin for oor teams tae ensure that they are familiar wi the platform an can effectively uitilise it. There micht an aw be some initial costs tae muive oor current infrastructur tae the AWS platform. Ownership The responsibility for ensurin the effective uitilisation o AWS an the management o associatit risks will fa within the remit o the cloud infrastructur team. Onie issues that arise maun be addressed bi this team. Review The decisioun tae adopt AWS will be reviewed on an annual basis tae ensure that it continues tae meet oor needs an that the benefits o the platform are bein fully realised.

records.title: Architectur Decisioun Record: API uisin JSON v. gRPC
headings: Architectur Decisioun Record: API uisin JSON v. gRPC
records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record: API uisin JSON v. gRPC Status Accepted Context We are designin an API for a new service that will be uised bi multiple clients. We hae been considerin twa options for implementin the API: uisin JSON ower HTTP or uisin gRPC. JSON ower HTTP is a widely-uised approach for biggin APIs, an it is supportit bi mony programmin leids an frameworks. This approach is simple, lichtwecht, an easy tae unnerstaun, makin it a guid chyce for mony projects. But, it can be less efficient than ither options, especially whan it comes tae haunlin muckle amoonts o data. gRPC, on the ither haun, is a newer technology that offers a mair efficient wey o biggin APIs. It uises binary serialisation tae transfer data, which can be faster an mair compact than uisin JSON. gRPC an aw supports bidirectional streamin, makin it a guid chyce for real-time applications. Decision Efter considerin the pros an cons o baith options, we hae decidit tae uise gRPC for oor API. Tho JSON ower HTTP is a simpler option, we believe that gRPC will provide a mair efficient an scalable solution for oor service. We an aw anticipate that oor API will haunle a muckle amoont o data, an gRPC's binary serialisation will be mair efficient for this uise case. In addition, we believe that gRPC's support for bidirectional streamin will be beneficial for real-time applications that we micht develop in the future. Consequences Bi chuisin gRPC, we will need tae uise a different set o tuils an leebraries tae big oor API compared tae uisin JSON ower HTTP. This micht require additional time an effort tae lairn an implement thir technologies. Additionally, clients wha want tae uise oor API will need tae uise gRPC-compatible leebraries, which micht no be as widely supportit as JSON ower HTTP leebraries. But, we believe that the benefits o uisin gRPC outweigh thir potential drawbacks, an we are confident that this decisioun will result in a mair efficient an scalable API.

records.title: browser-automatioun-framewark-for-e2e-testin-playwright-versus-selenium
headings: Architectur decisioun record: browser automatioun framewark for E2E testin (Playwright vs Selenium)
records.text: Architectur decisioun record: browser automatioun framewark for E2E testin (Playwright vs Selenium) Context We are in the process o selectin a browser automatioun framewark for oor end-tae-end (E2E) testin pipeline. This framewark will be integral tae oor CI/CD processes, rinnin tests that simulate real uiser interactiouns on oor platform. Specifically, the tests will cover scenarios sic as uiser sign-up/sign-in, file uploads, dashboard interactiouns, an report doonloads. As a startup , oor focus is on agile develapment , wi a need tae rapidly iterate an evolve. Oor team predominantly warks wi TypeScript an Python , an the ability tae screive tests in thir leids is essential. Additionally, the platform contains interactive chairts an dashboards , which maks it critical that the automatioun tuil supports rich, dynamic UIs weel. The twa contenders for this task are Playwright an Selenium , each wi its strengths an trade-offs. We need tae evaluate thir frameworks based on the features an requirements outlined ablow. Considered Options Playwright (by Microsoft) Selenium (by the Selenium Project) Decision Drivers The factors influencin oor decisioun are as follaes: Agile Development : The chosen tuil maun enable fast, flexible develapment cycles. Language Support : Oor team requires support for baith TypeScript an Python . Interactive UI Testing : The ability tae test interactive chairts, dashboards, an dynamic elements reliably is essential. Runtime Speed : While no a primary concern, performance in CI/CD pipelines is a consideration. Scalability : We are no plannin for muckle scalin in the immediate future, but we want tae ensure the solution can haunle future growth. Backwards Compatibility : Legacy systems an compatibility wi aulder browsers arena critical for oor project at this time. Mobile Testing : While no an immediate focus, the framewark sud be capable o testin mobile-responsive features or be extensible for sic uise cases. Multi-monitor Testing : Support for multi-monitor configuratiouns is a secondary requirement, especially if we ever scale tae testin for mair complex uiser workflows. File Upload Testing : The framewark maun haunle file uploads efficiently, a core requirement o oor testin needs. Evaluation Criteria Ease of Use : Hoo easy is it tae screive an keep up tests? Language Support : Daes the framewark support TypeScript an Python, the twa leids oor team uises maist frequently? Interactive UI Testing : Hoo weel daes the framewark haunle complex, interactive uiser interfaces sic as chairts, file uploads, an dynamic data? CI/CD Integration : Hoo weel daes the framewark integrate intae common CI/CD tuils an services? Cross-browser Support : Whit browsers are supportit an hoo weel dae they perform? Performance and Speed : Hoo quickly dae tests rin, especially in a CI/CD pipeline? Scalability : Hoo weel can the framewark scale if mair tests or mair complex scenarios are addit? Community and Ecosystem : Hoo active is the framewark's community? Are there plenty o integratiouns an extensiouns available? Considerations 5.1 Playwright Pros : Smarter API for Local File Uploads : Playwright’s API for interactin wi local files an performin file uploads is simpler an mair intuitive. This wud mak file upload testin easier tae implement an keep up. Syntax and Code Generation : Playwright haes a shorter, mair concise syntax. This results in less boilerplate code, which improves maintainability an developer efficiency. Additionally, this shorter syntax improves OpenAI code generation quality, makin it easier tae automatically generate test scripts. Interactive UI Testing : Playwright excels at testin dynamic, interactive wab applications, sic as thae wi rich chairts, complex uiser interactiouns, an real-time updates. It haunles WebSockets, WebRTC, shadow DOMs, an ither modern wab technologies unco effectively. Cross-browser Support : Playwright supports Chromium , WebKit , an Firefox . It haes consistent performance athort thir browsers, which sud cover maist o oor testin needs. CI/CD Integration : Playwright integrates seamlessly wi modern CI/CD platforms (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.). It can rin tests in parallel athort different browsers, optimisin test rin times an makin it suitable for rapid develapment. Fast and Reliable : Playwright is faster than Selenium in general, especially in headless mode, an mair resilient whan dealin wi asynchronous wab elements. Cons : Limited Mobile Testing : While Playwright daes support mobile emulation for browsers, it lacks native mobile testin capabilities like Selenium’s integratioun wi Appium for true mobile testin. Smaller Ecosystem : Playwright is still newer an less establisht than Selenium. While it haes a rapidly growin community an guid documentation, it micht no yet hae the vast ecosystem o plugins an integratiouns that Selenium offers. Limited Browser Support : While Playwright covers the major modern browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox), its support for legacy browsers (e.g., Internet Explorer) isna as robust as Selenium’s. 5.2 Selenium Pros : Longer History and Maturity : Selenium haes been roun for a lang time an haes a pruved track record. It’s widely uised athort mony teams an industries, which haes led tae a vast ecosystem o plugins, integratiouns, an resources. Cross-browser and Cross-platform Support : Selenium supports a wide variety of browsers an versiouns, includin Internet Explorer , an can an aw be integratit wi various tuils like Docker , Selenium Grid , an cloud services for distributit testin. Mobile Testing : Selenium, throu its integratioun wi Appium , is muckle mair robust for mobile testin, includin baith Android an iOS applications. This maks it the better chyce for projects wi a mobile-first or mobile-heavy focus. Multi-monitor Testing : Selenium provides better support for scenarios involvin multiple monitors or complex multi-window interactiouns. Cons : Complexity : Selenium’s API is mair verbose an explicit. While this can be an advantage in some cases, it means mair code tae screive an keep up, which micht reduce developer agility—especially important in a startup environment. Performance : Selenium generally rins slawer than Playwright, especially in headless mode. This could impact CI/CD pipelines, particularly as the nummer o tests growes. Interactive UI Testing : Selenium isna as smooth as Playwright whan it comes tae testin modern, interactive wab UIs, particularly wi chairts an real-time data updates. It requires mair setup an haunlin tae reliably interact wi dynamic content. Comparison Summary Feature Playwright Selenium ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------- Ease of Use Shorter syntax, mair intuitive for modern UIs Mair explicit, requires mair boilerplate Language Support TypeScript, Python, JavaScript TypeScript, Python, Java, Ruby, C# Interactive UI Testing Excellent for dynamic, real-time UIs Haunles basic UIs, but mair verbose an complex for rich interactiouns File Upload Testing Smarter API for file uploads Mair verbose, less intuitive API CI/CD Integration Easy integratioun wi GitHub Actions, Jenkins Strang integratioun wi mony CI tuils Mobile Testing Limitit, juist emulation Full support throu Appium Cross-browser Support Chromium, WebKit, Firefox Full support athort major an legacy browsers Performance Fast, optimised for headless testin Slawer, especially in headless mode Multi-monitor Testing Limitit Guid support for multi-monitor setups Community and Ecosystem Growin, guid documentation Lairge, mature, extensive ecosystem Decision Efter considerin the requirements an trade-offs, Playwright is the better chyce for oor current needs. Its smarter API for local file upload testin, concise syntax, an strang support for interactive UI testin mak it an ideal fit for oor agile develapment cycle. The fact that it supports baith TypeScript an Python is critical for oor team, an the framewark's modern approach tae testin will let us screive clean, maintainable code. While Selenium bides a great tuil, particularly for mobile testin, legacy browser support, an multi-monitor setups, it is less weel-suitit tae oor current needs. Its verbosity, slawer performance, an mair complex haunlin o dynamic UIs like chairts mak it less optimal for oor uise case. Consequences Immediate Action : We will adopt Playwright for oor E2E testin, focusin on testin uiser flows involvin sign-up, sign-in, file uploads, dashboards, an report doonloads. Long-Term Considerations : We will keep an ee on the evolvin Playwright ecosystem. If oor needs chynge, particularly aroun mobile testin or support for legacy browsers, we micht revisit Selenium. Training and Documentation : Develapment teams will need tae become familiar wi Playwright's API, particularly for haunlin dynamic UIs an file uploads. Migration : Existin Selenium tests (if onie) will be gradually migratit tae Playwright. Future Considerations

records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record: chairt leebrary toolkit for data veesualisin uisin TypeScript an JSON Primary Objective: Tae select an advanced chairtin toolkit for makin interactive veesualisatiouns, focusin on financial data, scientific data, an government data uisin TypeScript an JSON. The leebrary sud provide robust features, flexibility, an be open-source. Context an Requirements: Agile Development (High Priority) : As a startup, quick iteration, prototypin, an flexibility in develapment are essential. The chairt leebrary maun allou for fast develapment cycles. Chart Types (High Priority) : Doughnut Chairt Radar Chairt Clustering Process Chairt Area Chairt wi Time Axis Candlestick Chairt Nightingale Chairt Geo SVG Map Thir chairt types are specifically important for veesualisin complex datasets, sic as financial trends, scientific metrics, an geographical information. Free and Open Source (High Priority) : The toolkit sud be open-source tae avoid licensin costs, provide transparency, an offer flexibility for customisation. Low Importance Criteria : Runtime Speed : While performance is important, it isna a tap priority for this decisioun. Scalability : Tho scalability is generally important, the immediate need is tae big an MVP that micht growe ower time. Scalability concerns can be addressed efter. Backwards Compatibility : No a primary concern for the initial build, sae lang as the leebrary is modern an actively keepit up. Leebraries Evaluatit: Apache ECharts Chart.js ApexCharts AG Charts Highcharts Carbon Charts Layer Cake D3.js --- Apache ECharts Overview : Apache ECharts is a pouerfu, flexible chairtin leebrary for interactive, customisable veesualisatiouns. It provides support for a braid variety o chairts an is particularly strang in complex, dynamic veesualisatiouns. Strengths : Advanced Interactivity : ECharts excels in providin interactive chairts, offerin features like zoomin, pannin, an dynamic data updates. Doughnut, Radar, Candlestick, Geo SVG Maps : ECharts supports mony o the required chairt types, includin doughnut, radar, candlestick, an geographical map veesualisatiouns. Free and Open Source : ECharts is an open-source leebrary, which fits the budget-conscious nature o a startup an provides freedom tae modify the code. Flexibility and Extensibility : Heichly customisable, wi extensive support for animatiouns, custom veesualisatiouns, an advanced chairtin techniques. Weaknesses : Learning Curve : ECharts, while pouerfu, can hae a steeper learnin curve due tae its flexibility an extensive API. Documentation Complexity : The documentation is comprehensive but can be owerwhelmin for developers juist stairtin oot wi it. Verdict : ECharts is heichly suitable for the project due tae its support for interactive chairts, includin aw the required types like candlestick chairts, radar chairts, an geo maps. Its open-source nature aligns wi the project's need for flexibility an cost-effectiveness. --- Chart.js Overview : Chart.js is a simple, easy-tae-uise chairtin leebrary for biggin common chairt types. It’s kent for its simplicity an ease o integratioun. Strengths : Ease of Use : Chart.js is unco simple tae set up an uise, wi a minimal learnin curve. Open Source : Chart.js is free an open-source, which is critical for reducin costs. Common Chart Types : It supports basic chairts like doughnut, area, radar, an line chairts, which cover maist o the primary needs. Weaknesses : Limited Advanced Charts : Chart.js daesna natively support complex chairt types like candlestick chairts, geo SVG maps, or clusterin process chairts. While thir features can be addit throu plugins or customisation, it isna as straichtforrit as wi ither leebraries. Interactivity : Tho Chart.js supports basic interactivity (e.g., tooltips an hover effects), it daesna offer as advanced features as ECharts or D3.js. Verdict : Chart.js is great for simple, quick projects, but its lack o support for complex chairt types maks it unsuitable for a data-heavy application wi advanced needs like candlestick chairts an geo maps. It’s a guid chyce for prototypin, but for the required chairt types, mair advanced tuils are recommendit. --- ApexCharts Overview : ApexCharts is a modern chairtin leebrary that provides a variety o chairt types an focuses on interactive veesualisatiouns wi an easy-tae-uise API. Strengths : Interactive Features : ApexCharts offers interactive chairts wi tooltips, zoomin, pannin, an updates. Support for Financial and Scientific Charts : It supports a braid variety o chairt types, includin candlestick chairts, radar chairts, an area chairts. Ease of Use : It haes a straichtforrit API an is simple tae integrate intae a project. Free and Open Source : ApexCharts offers a free open-source version that is suitable for mony uise cases. Weaknesses : Complex Customization : While it provides mony features, the customisation options arena as flexible as ECharts or D3.js for heichly complex or custom chairtin needs. Geo Maps : ApexCharts daesna natively support geo maps or clusterin process chairts, which are required for this project. Verdict : ApexCharts is a strang contender due tae its ease o uise an interactivity, but it fa's short on certain advanced chairt types, particularly the need for geo maps an clusterin chairts. It’s a guid option for simpler chairts but lacks some required features. --- AG Charts Overview : AG Charts is a commercial-grade chairtin leebrary designed for performance an precision. It is heichly suitable for makin financial, scientific, an business dashboards. Strengths : Advanced Chart Types : AG Charts supports mony advanced chairt types, includin candlestick chairts, area chairts, radar chairts, an mair. It an aw offers deep integratioun wi ither AG-Grid products. High Performance : It offers excellent performance, especially whan dealin wi lairge datasets. Interactivity : AG Charts supports a variety o interactive features like zoomin, tooltips, an dynamic updates. Weaknesses : Not Fully Free : While AG Charts offers a free version, the full-featurit version is paid, which could be a barrier for startups leukin tae minimise costs. Complexity : While the leebrary is feature-rich, it micht be owerkill for simpler projects an can require mair setup an configuratioun compared tae ither options. Verdict : AG Charts is pouerfu an feature-rich but micht no be the best fit due tae its commercial nature an cost structur. Its suitability depends on whether the budget can accommodate paid versiouns or if open-source alternatives are preferred. --- Highcharts Overview : Highcharts is a popular chairtin leebrary kent for its braid range o chairt types an pouerfu customisation options. Strengths : Comprehensive Chart Types : Highcharts supports a braid variety o chairts, includin candlestick, radar, area, an geo maps. Interactive and Dynamic : Highcharts provides rich interactive features, includin drill-doons, zoomin, an pannin. Ease of Use : It haes a user-friendly API an guid documentation, makin it easy tae get stairtit. Weaknesses : Commercial License : While Highcharts offers a free version for non-commercial uise, the commercial licence is expensive, which could be a significant drawback for startups. Learning Curve : Tho no as steep as ECharts, the learnin curve for Highcharts can still be challengin for beginners. Verdict : Highcharts is a feature-rich leebrary, but its commercial licensin maks it less suitable for open-source, cost-sensitive projects. Its comprehensive chairtin options are a plus, but the licensin issue limits its appeal for this uise case. --- Carbon Charts Overview : Carbon Charts is a chairtin leebrary developit bi IBM, designed for makin visually appealin an heichly customisable chairts. Strengths : Customizability : Carbon Charts allous for extensive customisation o chairt appearance an behaviour. Open Source : It is free an open-source, which aligns wi the project’s requirement for budget-friendly solutiouns. Support for Common Charts : It supports common chairt types like doughnut, radar, an area chairts, tho it lacks support for mair advanced types like geo maps or candlestick chairts. Weaknesses : Limited Advanced Chart Types : It daesna support geo maps, clusterin process chairts, or candlestick chairts, which are essential for the project. Smaller Ecosystem : Carbon Charts haes a smaller community an ecosystem compared tae lairger chairt leebraries like ECharts or Highcharts. Verdict : Carbon Charts is open-source an customisable but lacks support for the mair complex chairt types needit for this project. It is mair suitable for simpler chairtin needs. --- Layer Cake Overview : Layer Cake is a data veesualisatioun leebrary designed for makin flexible, layered veesualisatiouns. Strengths : Customizable Layers : It provides pouerfu layerin options for complex veesualisatiouns. Open Source : It’s free an open-source, makin it a viable option for budget-conscious projects. Weaknesses : Limited Documentation : Layer Cake lacks extensive documentation an community support, makin it mair difficult tae wark wi compared tae mair establisht leebraries. Not Built for Charts : Layer Cake is better suitit tae non-chairt veesualisatiouns, sae its oot-o-the-box chairtin options are limitit. Verdict : While interestin for unique veesualisatiouns, Layer Cake isna ideal for traditional chairtin requirements like candlestick chairts or radar chairts. It’s mair suitit tae custom veesualisatiouns ootside the scope o staundart chairts. --- D3.js Overview : D3.js is a pouerfu JavaScript leebrary for makin data-driven veesualisatiouns throu HTML, SVG, an CSS. Strengths : Unmatched Flexibility : D3.js lets ye mak virtually onie type o custom veesualisatioun, makin it heichly pouerfu for advanced an interactive chairts. Extensive Features : It supports aw chairt types required, includin geo maps, clusterin chairts, an mair. Customizable : The level o customisation in D3.js is unparalleled, lettin developers big heichly tailored veesualisatiouns. Weaknesses : Steep Learning Curve : D3.js haes a steep learnin curve an is mair complex tae integrate compared tae ither leebraries. Time-Consuming : Biggin chairts in D3.js can be time-consumin, especially for common chairts like candlestick or doughnut chairts. Verdict : D3.js is incredibly pouerfu for advanced, customisit chairts but is owerkill for mony typical uise cases due tae its steep learnin curve an develapment time. It’s best for situatiouns whaur the ither chairt leebraries dinnae provide the required level o customisation. --- Conclusion Efter evaluatin the leebraries based on the project’s needs, Apache ECharts staunds oot as the best option. It supports the full range o required chairts, includin geo maps, candlestick chairts, an clusterin chairts. It’s open-source, feature-rich, an heichly interactive, which aligns perfectly wi the project's goals. While D3.js offers the maist flexibility, its complexity an time investment mak it less ideal for a startup leukin tae iterate quickly. ApexCharts an Chart.js are guid alternatives for simpler projects but lack support for advanced chairt types.

records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record: authenticatioun authorisatioun options Wab application authenticatioun an authorisatioun are twa crucial concepts in securin access tae applications an services. Baith deal wi the identity o uisers an hoo permissiouns are grantit, but they focus on different aspects: Authentication is the process o verifyin the identity o a uiser or system. Authorization is the process o determinin whit resources or actiouns the authenticatit uiser or system can access. Noo, let's dive intae the specific protocols an technologies ye've mentioned, which are commonly uised in modern wab applications for managin authenticatioun an authorisatioun. OAuth (Open Authorization) OAuth is an open staundart for authorisatioun. It lets a uiser grant a third-pairty application limitit access tae their resources athoot sharin their credentials. The key idea is delegated access . OAuth is aften uised in situatiouns whaur uisers can log in tae a third-pairty service (e.g., signin in wi Google) athoot directly providin their uisername an passwird tae the third-pairty. Flow : OAuth typically follaes a token-based flow, whaur an authorisatioun server issues an access token tae the third-pairty application. This token represents the uiser's permissiouns, an the application uises it tae access the uiser's data or resources frae an API. Example : A uiser signs intae a third-pairty app uisin their Google account. Google verifies the uiser's identity an than grants a token that lets the third-pairty app access some Google data (e.g., Google Calendar). OAuth does not haunle authenticatioun directly; it’s aboot grantin access. For authenticatioun, OAuth is aften pairit wi ither protocols, like OpenID Connect . OpenID Connect (OIDC) OpenID Connect (OIDC) is an identity layer biggit on tap o OAuth 2.0 that adds authenticatioun tae OAuth’s authorisatioun capabilities. Essentially, OpenID Connect extends OAuth tae haunle user authentication an provides a staundartised wey for applications tae verify the identity o a uiser. Flow : Whan a uiser logs in uisin OpenID Connect, the third-pairty application requests an ID token (in addition tae the OAuth access token). The ID token contains information aboot the uiser (sic as their uisername, email, an ither claims). This lets the application ken wha the uiser is an whether they are authenticatit. Example : Loggin intae a service like Slack uisin yer Google account (Google bein the OpenID Connect provider) involves authenticatioun via OpenID Connect, while OAuth manages the access tae yer Google resources. OIDC maks it easier for third-pairty apps tae authenticate users while still allouin fine-grained control ower whit resources thae apps can access. SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) SAML is an aulder, XML-based staundart uised for exchangin authenticatioun an authorisatioun data atween pairties, particularly in Single Sign-On (SSO) scenarios. It's primarily uised in enterprise environments tae let uisers authenticate ance an access multiple applications athoot re-enterin credentials. Flow : The uiser first authenticates wi an identity provider (IdP). The IdP generates a signed SAML assertion that includes the uiser's identity an relatit attributes. The assertion is sent tae the service provider (SP), which uises it tae authorise access tae the application. Example : An employee logs intae their corporate portal (the IdP) an is automatically loggit intae ither systems like email, CRM, etc., athoot re-enterin credentials. The authenticatioun process is based on the SAML assertion sent bi the IdP. SAML is commonly uised in enterprise SSO solutions an warks weel for wab applications in corporate environments, but it’s less mobile-friendly compared tae OAuth/OIDC. WS-Federation (Web Services Federation) WS-Federation is anither protocol uised for Single Sign-On (SSO) , especially in Microsoft-based enterprise environments. It's pairt o the WS- (Web Services) faimily o specificatiouns an allous for identity federation athort different security domains (sic as atween different organisatiouns or atween different services). Flow : WS-Federation lets a trusted identity provider (IdP) authenticate uisers an issue tokens that the service provider can uise for authorisatioun. It’s similar tae SAML but is aften uised in scenarios that rely heavily on Microsoft technologies. Example : A uiser logs intae an enterprise application hostit bi Microsoft Azure Active Directory (AD), an their identity can be uised tae access ither federatit services, includin applications hostit bi third-pairty vendors. Tho WS-Federation is largely replacit bi newer protocols like OAuth2.0 an OpenID Connect in mony modern wab environments, it’s still uised in legacy systems, especially in Microsoft-centric enterprises. LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) LDAP is a protocol uised tae access an manage directory services, commonly uised for storing user credentials an managin access control in a centralised directory (aften cried a Directory Service ). LDAP isna specifically aboot authenticatioun or authorisatioun but is uised tae store an retrieve identity data, which is than uised in thae processes. Authentication : LDAP lets an application authenticate uisers bi queryin the directory service for credentials (like passwirds). Authorization : It an aw manages uiser roles an permissiouns, helpin determine whether a uiser haes access tae certain resources. Example : Mony enterprises uise LDAP-based directories (e.g., Active Directory ) for authenticatioun an authorisatioun, especially within Windows environments. LDAP is crucial for enterprises tae manage uiser access athort internal systems, but in a modern wab context, LDAP is aften integratit wi ither protocols like SAML or OAuth for mair complete identity management. Social SSO Providers Social Single Sign-On (SSO) providers like Facebook , Google , Twitter , GitHub , an ithers allou uisers tae authenticate intae third-pairty applications uisin their social media credentials. This is a type o OAuth-based authentication whaur the third-pairty service (e.g., Google) is the identity provider. Flow : The uiser clicks "Log in with Google" (for example). The app redirects tae Google, whaur the uiser logs in (if no awready loggit in). Google than provides an access token or ID token tae the third-pairty app, which can be uised tae authenticate the uiser an possibly access their data. Example : Mony applications let ye log in uisin yer Google or Facebook credentials. The app will uise OAuth or OpenID Connect ahint the scenes tae verify yer identity an, in some cases, access certain social media data. Social SSO is a convenient an widely adoptit method for authenticatioun acause it reduces friction for uisers, wha micht no want tae mak yet anither uisername an passwird. --- Summary o Differences: OAuth : Uised for authorisatioun, lets third-pairty apps access uiser data athoot exposin credentials. OpenID Connect : Extends OAuth tae provide authenticatioun, lettin apps verify uiser identity. SAML : XML-based protocol uised for SSO, aften in enterprise environments. WS-Federation : A Microsoft-specific protocol for identity federation, uised in legacy systems. LDAP : A protocol for queryin directory services tae authenticate uisers an manage authorisatioun. Social SSO Providers : OAuth-based systems (like Google, Facebook) that let third-pairty apps authenticate uisers uisin their social media credentials. Each o thir technologies haes its ain strengths an uise cases, an in modern applications, ye micht see a combination o them bein uised for different aspects o security (e.g., OAuth/OIDC for API access, SAML for enterprise SSO).

records.text: Decisioun Record for continuous integratioun Title: Decisioun tae Implement Continuous Integratioun Context The company haes been experiencin challenges wi the develapment process as a result o manual testin, build processes, an deployments. records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record: CSS framewark Contents: Soummary Maitter Decisioun Staunin Pairticulars Assumptiouns Limitatiouns Positiouns Argiment Implicatiouns Relatit Relatit decisiouns Relatit requirements Relatit artefacts Relatit principles Jottins Soummary Maitter We want tae uise a CSS framewark tae mak oor wab applications: We want user experience tae be fast an reliable, on aw popular browsers an screen sizes. We want rapid iteration on design, layout, UI/UX, etc. We want responsive applications, especially for smaller screens sic as on mobile devices, larger screens sic as on 4K widescreens, an dynamic screens sic as rotatable displays. Decisioun Decidit on Bulma. Staunin Decidit on Bulma. Open tae new CSS framewark chyces as they arrive. Pairticulars Assumptiouns We want tae mak wab apps that are modern, fast, reliable, responsive, etc. Typical modern wab apps are reducin/eliminatin the uise o jQuery acause o multiple reasons: Modern JavaScript is phasin in mony capabilities that jQuery haes providit, sae jQuery is less needit, an there are better/faster/smaller modules that provide specific implementatiouns jQuery's braid approach is tae dae direct DOM manipulation, which is an anti-pattern for modern JavaScript frameworks (e.g. React, Vue, Svelte) jQuery interferes wi itsel if it's loadit twice, etc. Limitatiouns If we chuise a CSS framewark that uises jQuery, than we're stuck importin jQuery. For example, Semantic UI uises jQuery, an Tachyons daesna. If we chuise a CSS framewark that is minimal, than we forgae framewark components that we micht want noo or sune. For example, Semantic UI provides an image carousel, an Tachyons daesna. Positiouns We consideret uisin nae framewark. This still seems viable, especially acause CSS grid provides muckle o whit we need for oor project.. We consideret mony CSS frameworks uisin a quick shortlist triage: Bootstrap, Bulma, Foundation, Materialize, Semantic UI, Tachyons, etc. Oor twa selectiouns for deeper review are Semantic UI (acause it haes the maist-semantic approach) an Bulma (acause it haes the lichtest-wecht approach that provides the components we want noo). We consideret Semantic UI. This provides mony components, includin anes we want for oor project: tabs, grids, buttons, etc. We did a pilot wi Semantic UI twa weys: uisin typical CDN files, an uisin NPM repos. We achieved success wi Semantic UI in a static HTML page, but didna achieve success within oor timebox tae big a JavaScript SPA (primarily acause o jQuery load issues). We discoverit that ither coders hae been askin the Semantic UI developers tae mak a jQuery-free version, for the same reasons we hae. Ither coders hae been requestin a jQuery-free version for mony years, yet the developers hae said nae, an statit that onie jQuery-free version wud be ower hard tae screive e.g. "the Semantic UI project has more than 22,000 touchpoints that use jQuery". Example wi Semantic: Alpha Bravo We consideret Bulma. Bulma haes mony similar capabilities as Semantic UI, tho no as mony sophisticatit components. records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record: Microsoft Azure cloud infrastructur" Decision Title: Adoptin Microsoft Azure as the cloud infrastructur for oor organisation Decision Maker: Chief Information Officer Date: 2021-10-15 Status: Approved Background The organisation is plannin tae migrate frae traditional on-premises infrastructur tae cloud infrastructur. In order tae achieve this, the organisation haes evaluatit multiple cloud service providers sic as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Microsoft Azure, an IBM Cloud. Each provider haes its ain set o features, benefits, an pricin structur. Efter a detailed analysis, it wis concludit that Microsoft Azure is the maist suitable option for oor organisation. Rationale The follaein are the reasons for adoptin Microsoft Azure: Comprehensive Services: Azure provides a complete range o cloud services frae infrastructur as a service (IaaS) tae saftware as a service (SaaS) an platform as a service (PaaS). Cost-effective: Azure offers a pay-as-ye-gae pricin model, which means we juist pay for the resources uised. This helps us save costs when compared tae traditional on-premises infrastructur. Conclusion Adoptin Microsoft Azure as the cloud infrastructur for oor organisation aligns wi oor business requirements an offers several benefits sic as scalability, flexibility, security, an cost-effectiveness. records.title: Microsoft Azure DevOps
headings: Microsoft Devops CI: An Unsatisfying Adventure
records.text: Microsoft Azure DevOps Contents: Soummary Maitter Decisioun Staunin Pairticulars Assumptiouns Limitatiouns Positiouns Argiment Implicatiouns Relatit Relatit decisiouns Relatit requirements Relatit artefacts Relatit principles Jottins Microsoft Devops CI: An Unsatisfying Adventure Hacker News discussion highlichts Windows Develapment MVP Edward Thomson (Azure PM) summary Soummary Maitter We want tae uise devops tae big, integrate, deploy, an host oor projects. We are considerin Microsoft Azure DevOps. We want developer experience tae be fast an reliable, for the setup o the devops e.g. configurin as weel as ongoin uise e.g. fast build times. We want tae consider uisin Microsoft Azure as haill, for hostin the project apps, databaises, etc. Decisioun Decidit against Microsoft Azure DevOps. Staunin Decidit. Open tae revisitin if/whan new significant info arrives. Pairticulars Assumptiouns Aw the usual devops assumptiouns, sic as in the beuk Accelerate. Fast builds are a significant help. This accelerates the feedback loops. We can swap in/oot pieces frae alternate vendors i.e. we micht want tae bring oor ain heicher-speed build servers, or uise oor ain chyce o version control system, or coordinate wi a self-hostit continuous integratioun server. Streamlined uisability is a significant help, for developer experience, an in turn for subtle areas sic as consistency, clarity, security, an ease o learnin curve. Whan onie thing is broken or problematic, we want an effective wey tae report the issue. This is especially important for onie security-relatit issues. Limitatiouns Nane kent. Azure haes a publisht commitment tae playin weel wi external tuils. Positiouns We consideret uisin Microsoft Azure Devops vs. AWS which is incumbent. We experimentit wi Azure DevOps, Azure Pipelines, Azure Repo, an Azure spin up o new server via Terraform. We experimentit wi gettin support frae Microsoft representatives. We gaithered information frae peers on blogs an Hacker News. Argiment Azure DevOps advertises an excellent set o offerins, but they dinnae haud up, an they dinnae wark weel thegither, an support is puir. Oor firsthaun experience: Azure setup is a mess o UIs, some o which owerlap wi Microsoft accounts, some o which dinnae. E.g. there's an Azure sign in, a Microsoft.com sign in, a Live.com sign in, etc. an aw are simultaneously in play. We come athort a minor security issue durin setup, an foond nae resolution. We tried mony weys tae report it, tae mony Microsoft reps, wi nae success. We successfully reportit it tae Microsoft security, which replied wi won't fix. Documentation is aften either wrang or oot o date. At least some o this is due tae Microsoft's puir search engine, an some o this is due tae sub-par SEO. Terraform setup is weel documentit, an warks. But, Terraform supoprt is weak compared tae AWS acause Microsoft is biggin business relationships wi vendors tae dae chain-throu Terraform setup examples. Oor peer experiences: Efter we did oor ain blind assessment, we leukit for peer experiences. Whit we foond confirmed oor experiences. Peers reportit additional problems wi build times, an problems wi bring-yer-ain-build server. Thir problems are significantly mair severe than UI problems, acause daein builds is the core purpose o a build pipeline, an we expect tae dae mony per day. We foond excellent participation bi Azure teammates in the discussion areas. Kudos tae Microsoft for this. We are especially impressit wi Edward Thomson, Azure PM an coder, acause o his participation, directness, an technical explanatiouns. Implicatiouns Chuisin Microsoft Azure DevOps leuks likely tae be mair expensive ( 3x) in time an cost than no chuisin Azure. Relatit Relatit decisiouns If we chuise Azure DevOps, there are mony relatit offerins, includin Azure Repo, Azure Pipeline, etc. We believe that if we chuise Azure Devops, this micht mak it easier tae uise mair Azure capabilities, or micht mak it harder tae uise ither vendors' capabilities. We believe that Microsoft is makin great strides in developer experience, an we see Microsoft makin lairge acquisition o developer tuils (e.g. GitHub) an dependencies (e.g. Citus). If we chuise Azure DevOps, than we micht want tae emphasise chuisin the Microsoft acquisition offerins, an we micht an aw want tae approach the acquisition offerins wi mair care/assessement acause o potential tissue-rejection e.g. staff turnower risk. Relatit requirements We want build times tae be unco fast. We accept payin a heich premium for this. This is acause we want tae iterate unco fast. We want reliability tae be unco heich. We accept payin a heich premium for this. This is acause we are testin heich-value uise cases, includin financial transations, confidential transactiouns, etc. Oor tap 4 devops KPIs include mean time tae recovery, which necessitates fast builds an heich reliability. Relatit artefacts We want the build system tae output artefacts suitable for uisin in ither systems, sic as Artifactory. Relatit principles Easily reversible. We can evaluate Azure DevOps in parallel wi AWS incumbent. Jottins Microsoft Devops CI: An Unsatisfying Adventure https://toxicbakery.github.io/vsts-devops/microsoft-devops-ci/ Blog post. "As a saftware developer, I ken first-haun hoo difficult it is tae big quality products quickly an cheaply. It’s an art form that we whiles get richt, an ither times devolves intae somethin akin tae the Obama era healthcare government site. Oor level o control ower the resultin product varies, an blame for failure aften faas on the wrang fowk in the decisioun-makin hierarchy. Microsoft’s Azure DevOps (formerly kent as Visual Studio Team Services), despite clearly guid intentiouns, is a perfect storm o bad decisiouns an puir execution." Hacker News discussion highlichts https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=18983586 "We uise Azure DevOps extensively at my wark an, efter haein uised GitHub, Gitlab, self hostit solutiouns, Jenkins, TeamCity... Azure DevOps ranks deid last." "The UI is terribly clunky everywhaur. The warst for me are pull requests. Incredibly teuch tae wark wi fowk on a pull request. I canna even pynt ye tae "a" particular problem - for us it's broken everywhaur." "Azure Devops is somethin I want tae love. The UI keeps chyngin, but daesna fix unnerlyin bugs that hae been roun for ages." "The tuils arena weel integratit, the UI is really slaw, there’s nae dashboard view o active pull requests, builds, releases, etc for my favourite repos. Build/Deploy times are insanely slaw." "We tried tae an aw uise Azure Boards (Work Items, Boards, Backlogs, etc). Ouch. It is a complete UI mess o disjointit ideas. Instead o implementin ae thing weel, they implementit twa dizzen things terribly." Windows Develapment MVP Windows Develapment MVP here. I feel like I maun shouther some o the responsibility here for no bein louder aboot thir issues. But maun say, I'm disappointit tae hear ye're "surprised" aboot the UX issues. I've been tellin yer fowk the UX is dreadful (e.g. as faur back as pre-launch) an kept hearin back "we ken, we're fixin it". I'll stairt formalisin the feedback an push it throu the pipes, stay tuned. I'm an aw local (Bellevue), wud love tae come in an try tae pipeline oor relatively simple oss .net/wpf/uwp app. I suspect it'll be an ee opener for the baith o us. Some examples: Ye canna big a pipeline wi a git repo. that contains submodules Foond it impossible tae eedit the PATH for some custom tuilin The New Pipeline experience juist daesna mak a lot o sense, new uisers clickin roun will eventually end up at the wrang Docs. Edward Thomson (Azure PM) summary I wrate the code that merges yer pull requests. Program Manager for at Microsoft for Azure DevOps; formerly a saftware engineer on version control tuils at GitHub, Microsoft, SourceGear. https://www.edwardthomson.com/ Co-maintainer o libgit2. https://libgit2.github.io Co-host o All Things Git, the Podcast aboot Git. https://www.allthingsgit.com/ Curator o Developer Tools Weekly, a newsletter aboot develapment tuils. https://developertoolsweekly.com/

records.title: Monorepo versus multirepo
records.text: Monorepo versus multirepo Contents: Soummary Maitter Decisioun Staunin Pairticulars Assumptiouns Limitatiouns Positiouns Argiment Implicatiouns Relatit Relatit decisiouns Relatit requirements Relatit artefacts Relatit principles Jottins Soummary Maitter Oor project involves develapin three major categories o saftware: Front-end GUIs Middleware services Back-end servers Whan we develap, oor source code management (SCM) version control system (VCS) is git. We need tae chuise hoo we uise git tae organise oor code. The tap-level chyce is tae organise as a "monorepo" or "polyrepo" or "hybrid": Monorepo means we pit aw pieces intae ae muckle repo Polyrepo means we pit each piece in its ain repo Hybrid means some mix o monorepo an polyrepo For mair please see https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/monorepo-vs-polyrepo Decisioun Monorepo whan an organisation/team/project is relatively sma, an rapid iteration is heicher priority than sustainin stability. Polyrepo whan an organisation/team/project is relatively muckle, an sustainin stability is heicher priority than rapid iteration. Staunin Decidit. Open tae revisitin if/whan new tuilin becomes available for managin monorepos and/or polyrepos. Pairticulars Assumptiouns Aw the code that we're develapin is for ae organisation's offerins, an no for the general public. I.e. the Broker-Dealer isna aimin tae hae onie thing like general public volunteer developers. Limitatiouns Constraints are weel-documentit at https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/monorepo-vs-polyrepo Positiouns We consideret monorepos in the style o Google, Facebook, etc. We think onie monorepo scalin issues are sae faur in the future that we will be able tae leverage the same practices as Google an Facebook, bi the time we need them. We consideret polyrepos in the style o typical Git open source projects, sic as Google Android, Facebook React, etc. We think thir are the best chyce for general public participation (e.g. onieane in the warld can wark on the code) an individual availability (e.g. the project is uised on its ain, athoot onie ither pieces). Argiment Whan an organisation/team/project is relatively sma, we chuise monorepo, acause rapid iteration is significantly heicher in priority than sustainin stability Whan an organisation/team/project is relatively muckle, we chuise polyrepo, acause sustainin stability is significantly heicher in priority than rapid iteration. Implicatiouns If there's an existin pipeline for CI+CD, than we micht need tae adjust it for testin multiple projects within ae repo. CI+CD could tak mair time for a full build for a monorepo, acause CI+CD could big aw the projects in the monorepo. If an organisation/team/project growes, than a monorepo will hae scalin issues. Monorepo scalin issues micht mak it increasin valuable tae transition tae a polyrepo. Transition frae monorepo tae polyrepo is a significant devops task, an will need tae be plannit, managed, an programmed. Relatit Relatit decisiouns We will mak decisiouns for relatit tuilin tae manage monorepos (e.g. Google Bazel) an polyrepos (e.g. Lyft Refactorator). Relatit requirements We need tae develap the CI+CD pipeline tae wark weel wi git. Relatit artefacts We expect the repo organisation tae hae relatit artefacts for provisionin, configuration management, testin, an similar devops areas. Relatit principles Easily reversible. If the monorepo daesna wark in practice, or isna wantit bi leadership, it's simple tae chynge tae polyrepo. Customer Obsession. We value gettin the project in the hauns o customers, an we believe that a monoreop can get us there faster than a polyrepo, an an aw help us iterate faster. Think big. Google an Facebook are unco strang advocates for monorepos ower polyrepos, acause aw the core offerins can be develapit/testit/deployed in concert. Jottins Add onie notes here.

records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record: MySQL databaise Title: Chuisin MySQL as Databaise Management System for Project X Context an Problem Statement We need tae decide on which databaise management system (DBMS) tae uise for Project X. Conclusion Based on the available data an oor decisioun considerations, we believe that MySQL is the richt chyce for oor databaise management system for Project X. records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record: Pickin a Databaise Technologie Status Accepted Context We are designin a new application that requires storin an retrievin data in a scalable an performant manner. We hae identifiet three types o databaise technologies that are commonly uised: relational databaises, document databaises, an event databaises. Some applications are set tae uise local time, raither than UTC time. This can be convenient for projects that maun adjust tae local time, sic as projects that trigger events that are based on local time. Some systems hae different time precision needs an capabilities, sic as uisin a time resolution o seconds vs. milliseconds vs. nanoseconds. For example, the Linux operatin system date command uises a default time precision o seconds, whereas the Nasdaq stock exchange wants a default time precision o nanoseconds. Decisioun We chuise the timestamp staundart furm ISO 8601 wi nanosecond precision, specifically "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.NNNNNNNNNZ". The furm shaws the year, month, day, oor, minute, second, nanoseconds, an Zulu time zone a.k.a. UTC, GMT. Staunin Decidit. Pairticulars Assumptiouns We need tae haunle thir timestamp text strings, tae convert frae a timestamp tae a string (a.k.a. serialize) an convert frae a string tae a timestamp (a.k.a. deserialize). We want a furm that is generally easy tae uise, easy tae convert, an easy for a person tae read. We want compatibility wi a braid range o external systems that we canna control, sic as analytics systems, databaise systems, financial systems.
