records.text: Architectur Decisioun Record: wab application framewark, batteries includit, fu stack, for a stairtup product Primary Objective: Tae big a wab application for payin customers tae sign in, upload files, process data, an view reports, focusin on agile develapment, fu-stack functionality, an strang compatibility wi AI/ML tuils, especially Project Jupyter notebooks. Context an Requirements: Agile Development (High Priority) : As a startup, we need rapid iteration an flexibility. Agile practices, sic as quick prototypin, iterative develapment, an adaptability tae chynge, are key tae oor develapment cycle. Full-Stack Framework (High Priority) : We aim tae minimise owerheid bi selectin a framewark that can haunle baith backend an frontend efficiently, reducin the need for separate front-end frameworks. Compatibility with AI/ML Tools (High Priority) : The ability tae integrate easily wi data analysis tuils like Jupyter notebooks an Python's data science ecosystem (NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, etc.) is essential. This wud facilitate efficient data processin an reportin. Low Importance Criteria : Runtime Speed : While performance is relevant, it isna the maist critical factor at the stairt sin we are mair concernit wi develapment speed an feature completeness. Scalability : We anticipate growth, but scalability concerns can be addressed efter, an this isna a primary requirement richt noo. Backwards Compatibility : We are focusin on current technologies an arena heavily concernit aboot backward compatibility wi legacy systems. Frameworks Evaluatit: Django (Python) Ruby on Rails (Ruby) Phoenix (Elixir) Loco (Rust) --- Django (Python) Overview : Django is a heich-level wab framewark for Python that promotes rapid develapment an clean, pragmatic design. It is kent for its “batteries included” philosophy, meanin it includes mony features sic as authenticatioun, routin, ORM, an form haunlin richt oot o the box. Strengths : Full-Stack : Django is a comprehensive, fu-stack framewark that can haunle baith backend an frontend needs wi integratit features (e.g., templatin engine, admin interface). Agile Development : Django's weel-defined structur an conventiouns allou for rapid develapment an adaptability, crucial for a startup environment. The framewark comes wi excellent documentation an a rich ecosystem o third-pairty packages, which accelerates develapment. AI/ML Integration : Python's ecosystem is unmatched whan it comes tae data science an machine learnin. Django, bein Python-based, integrates seamlessly wi tuils like Jupyter notebooks, Pandas, NumPy, TensorFlow, an scikit-learn. Community and Ecosystem : Django haes an extensive community, robust documentation, an a braid range o plugins an extensiouns, which significantly speeds up develapment an troubleshootin. Weaknesses : Runtime Speed : Python tends tae be slawer compared tae leids like Rust or Elixir. But, for this uise case, whaur performance isna the primary concern, this micht no be a dealbreaker. Scalability : While Django is heichly scalable, there micht be challenges at the unco heich scale athoot carefu optimisation (e.g., whan haunlin heavy concurrent requests). But, Django can still be scaled effectively uisin load balancin an cachin techniques. Verdict : Django aligns weel wi the requirements for agile develapment, fu-stack support, an AI/ML compatibility. Its Python integratioun offers seamless access tae the data science tuils an leebraries necessary for the application. --- Ruby on Rails (Ruby) Overview : Ruby on Rails (RoR) is a mature, fu-stack wab application framewark kent for its convention-ower-configuratioun approach, which facilitates rapid develapment. Strengths : Full-Stack : RoR comes wi biggit-in tuils for baith backend an frontend develapment (e.g., views, templates, scaffoldin), an its rich leebrary o gems lets ye quickly implement various features. Agile Development : Ruby on Rails is particularly kent for its fast iteration cycles, which is advantageous for startups leukin tae quickly iterate on features. RoR supports test-driven develapment (TDD) an haes an establisht ecosystem for agile workflows. Community and Ecosystem : RoR haes a weel-establisht, strang community an a braid array o gems that can speed up develapment. Ease of Use : Rails haes a unco developer-friendly syntax an is kent for makin tasks sic as databaise migratiouns, model-view-controller (MVC) architectur, an route haunlin quick an simple. Weaknesses : Performance : Ruby tends tae hae slawer runtime performance compared tae Python or Elixir. While RoR can scale wi the richt infrastructur, Ruby’s performance micht become a bottleneck for applications that require heavy real-time processin or heich concurrent traffic. AI/ML Integration : Tho Ruby haes some machine learnin leebraries, it isna as widely adoptit in the AI/ML community as Python. Integratioun wi tuils like Jupyter notebooks isna as seamless, makin Python a stranger chyce for data-heavy applications. Verdict : While Ruby on Rails excels in agile develapment an rapid prototypin, it fa's short in terms o AI/ML compatibility compared tae Python (Django). It’s a viable chyce for startups that prioritise fast iteration ower deep data analysis integratioun. --- Phoenix (Elixir) Overview : Phoenix is a wab framewark biggit wi Elixir, a functional programmin leid designed for scalability an concurrency. Phoenix leverages the Erlang VM, which is kent for haunlin massive concurrency an fault-tolerant systems. Strengths : Scalability and Performance : Phoenix shines in scalability an haunlin heich concurrency. It is biggit on the Erlang VM, which can support thoosands (or even millions) o concurrent connectiouns, makin it a strang candidate for applications requirin real-time data processin or heich-volume traffic. Full-Stack : Phoenix includes everything needit tae big baith the backend an frontend o an application. It supports live views for interactive UI updates an includes a templatin engine. Agile Development : Phoenix is heichly modular, allouin for rapid iteration on features. It is weel-suitit tae startups that need tae muive quickly. AI/ML Compatibility : While Elixir haes emergin machine learnin leebraries, it isna as widely supportit for AI/ML tasks as Python. Integratin wi tuils like Jupyter notebooks wud require warkarounds, as Elixir’s ecosystem for data science isna as mature as Python’s. Weaknesses : AI/ML Ecosystem : Elixir isna the primary leid uised in data science or machine learnin, an the ecosystem isna as mature as Python’s. Sae, integratioun wi tuils like Jupyter notebooks or popular AI leebraries (TensorFlow, PyTorch) will be cumbersome. Learning Curve : If the team is unfamiliar wi functional programmin an Elixir, there micht be a steeper learnin curve. Verdict : Phoenix is an excellent chyce if scalability an concurrency are a primary concern. But, gien the priority on AI/ML compatibility, Phoenix micht no be the best fit due tae Elixir's limitit ecosystem in this space. --- Loco (Rust) Overview : Loco is a wab framewark biggit wi Rust, a systems programmin leid kent for its performance, memory safety, an concurrency. Rust is increasinly popular for biggin heich-performance applications. Strengths : Performance : Rust’s primary strength lies in its heich performance an memory safety, makin it an excellent chyce for applications requirin laich-level control or extremely heich performance. Concurrency : Rust’s ownership system ensures memory safety while allouin safe concurrent programmin, makin it ideal for systems that need tae scale efficiently an haunle parallelism. Weaknesses : Full-Stack Development : Loco, while promisin, isna as mature as the ither frameworks in terms o providin a complete fu-stack solution. It is mair suitable for backend develapment, an the front-end ecosystem roun Rust is still emergin. Agile Development : Develapin wi Rust can be slawer compared tae heicher-level leids like Python or Ruby due tae its laicher-level nature an steeper learnin curve. AI/ML Ecosystem : Rust daesna hae the same extensive ecosystem for AI/ML as Python. While there are growin leebraries in Rust for numerical computin, they are faur less mature than Python’s offerins, sic as Jupyter notebooks or machine learnin frameworks. Verdict : While Rust an its framewark Loco offer exceptional performance, the lack o fu-stack support, agile develapment benefits, an AI/ML ecosystem mak it less ideal for this specific uise case. It is mair suitit tae performance-critical applications raither than rapid wab develapment wi integratit data science tuils. --- Conclusion Efter evaluatin the options based on the project’s requirements, Django (Python) is the maist suitable chyce. It offers the follaein advantages: Full-Stack Capabilities : Django is a fu-stack framewark that integrates baith backend an frontend develapment. Agile Development : The framewark is weel-suitit tae rapid prototypin an iteration, which is essential for a startup environment. AI/ML Compatibility : Python is the leadin leid in AI/ML, an Django’s compatibility wi leebraries like Jupyter notebooks ensures smooth integratioun for data analysis an processin. Community and Ecosystem : Django’s strang community support an extensive leebrary ecosystem provide mony tuils tae accelerate develapment. While Ruby on Rails is an aw a strang contender for agile develapment, its limitit AI/ML support maks it less ideal for this specific uise case. Phoenix (Elixir) an Loco (Rust) , tho excellent for scalability an performance, fa' short in terms o AI/ML integratioun an fu-stack develapment. Therefore, Django is the recommendit framewark for this project.

records.text: Decisioun record for wark frae hame Title: Employees can wark frae hame Decision Maker: Management Team Decision Date: July 1, 2021 Background Acause o the ongoin COVID-19 pandemic, mony employees hae been warkin remotely frae hame. This arrangement haes providit benefits sic as increased flexibility, improved wark-life balance an a decrease in the spread o the virus. Furthermair, mony employees hae expressit that they wud like tae continue warkin frae hame even efter the pandemic haes endit. The policy applies tae aw full-time employees wha can effectively perform their duties frae hame an hae demonstratit success warkin remotely durin the pandemic. Eligible employees can chuise tae wark frae hame up tae three days per week, while in-office wark will be required for the remainin twa days. Tae ensure effective communication an collaboration, regular check-ins wi team members an managers will be required. Additionally, employees will be providit wi the necessary equipment an resources tae perform their duties effectively frae hame. The implementation o this policy will be reviewed an revisitit regularly tae ensure that it continues tae benefit baith the employees an the company. Reasoning The decisioun tae continue allouin employees tae wark frae hame is based on several factors, includin employee wark-life balance, greater flexibility an freedom, improved productivity, an less exposure tae the risk o infection. Bi implementin a flexible wark model, the company can attract an retain tap talent while an aw providin a positive company culture. Implicatiouns The implementation o the permanent wark frae hame policy will hae several implicatiouns, includin the need for ongoin communication an coordination amang team members, adjustin wark processes an protocols tae accommodate a remote warkforce, an ensurin that aw employees hae access tae the necessary equipment, tuils an resources. Conclusion The decisioun tae implement a permanent wark frae hame policy is in line wi the company's values o promotin a healthy wark-life balance, supportin employee well-bein an promotin a positive company culture. We believe that this decisioun will let oor organisation be mair agile an better suitit tae adapt tae chyngin business needs while improvin employee satisfaction an productivity.

records.text: Decisioun record templat bi arc42 Introduction an Goals Short description o the requirements, drivin forces, extract (or abstract) o requirements. Tap three (max five) quality goals for the architectur that hae the heichest priority for the major stakeholders. A table o important stakeholders wi their expectation regardin architectur. 1.1 Requirements Owerview Contents Short description o the functional requirements, drivin forces, extract (or abstract) o requirements. Links tae the (hopefully existin) requirements documents, wi information whaur tae find it. Motivation Frae the pynt o view o the end uisers a system is made or modified tae improve support o a business activity and/or improve the quality. Form Short textual description, probably in tabular uise-case format. If requirements documents exist this owerview sud refer tae thae documents. Keep thir excerpts as short as possible. Balance readability o this document wi potential redundancy w.r.t. requirements documents. 1.2 Quality goals Content The tap three (max five) quality goals for the architectur whase fulfilment is o heichest importance tae the major stakeholders. We really mean quality goals for the architectur. Dinnae confuse them wi project goals. They are no necessarily identical. The ISO 25010 staundart provides a nice owerview o potential topics o interest. Motivation Ye sud ken the quality goals o yer maist important stakeholders, sin they will influence fundamental architectural decisiouns. Mak siccar tae be unco concrete aboot thir qualities, avoid buzzwirds. If ye as an architect dinnae ken hoo the quality o yer wark will be judged … Form A table wi the maist important quality goals an concrete scenarios, ordered bi priorities. 1.3 Stakeholder Content Explicit owerview o stakeholders o the system, i.e. aw fowk, roles or organisations that sud ken the architectur hae tae be convinced o the architectur hae tae wark wi the architectur or wi code need the documentation o the architectur for their wark hae tae come up wi decisiouns aboot the system or its development Motivation Ye sud ken aw pairties involved in development o the system or affectit bi the system. Itherwise, ye micht get nesty surprises efter in the development process. Thir stakeholders determine the extent an the level o detail o yer wark an its results. Form Table wi role names, person names, an their expectatiouns wi respect tae the architectur an its documentation. Constraints Onie thing that constrains teams in design an implementation decisiouns or decisioun aboot relatit processes. Can whiles gae ayont individual systems an are valid for haill organisatiouns an companies. Content Onie requirement that constrains saftware architects in their freedom o design an implementation decisiouns or decisioun aboot the development process. Thir constraints whiles gae ayont individual systems an are valid for haill organisatiouns an companies. Motivation Architects sud ken exactly whaur they are free in their design decisiouns an whaur they maun adhere tae constraints. Constraints maun aye be dealt wi; they micht be negotiable, tho. Form Simple tables o constraints wi explanatiouns. If needit ye can subdivide them intae technical constraints, organisational an political constraints an conventiouns (e.g. programmin or versionin guidelines, documentation or namin conventiouns) Context an Scope Delimits yer system frae its (external) communication partners (neighbourin systems an uisers). Specifies the external interfaces. Shawn frae a business/domain perspective (aye) or a technical perspective (optional) Content System scope an context - as the name suggests - delimits yer system (i.e. yer scope) frae aw its communication partners (neighbourin systems an uisers, i.e. the context o yer system). It thereby specifies the external interfaces. If necessary, differentiate the business context (domain specific inputs an outputs) frae the technical context (channels, protocols, hardware). Motivation The domain interfaces an technical interfaces tae communication partners are amang yer system’s maist critical aspects. Mak siccar ye completely unnerstaun them. Form Various context diagrams Lists o communication partners an their interfaces. 3.1 Business context Content Specification o aw communication partners (uisers, IT-systems, …) wi explanatiouns o domain specific inputs an outputs or interfaces. Optionally ye can add domain specific formats or communication protocols. Motivation Aw stakeholders sud unnerstaun which data are exchanged wi the environment o the system. Form Aw kinds o diagrams that shaw the system as a black box an specify the domain interfaces tae communiations partners. Alternatively (or additionally) ye can uise a table. The title o the table is the name o yer system, the three columns contain the name o the communication partner, the inputs, an the outputs. 3.2 Technical context Contents Technical interfaces (channels an transmission media) linkin yer system tae its environment. In addition a mappin o domain specific input/output tae the channels, i.e. an explanation wi I/O uises which channel. Motivation Mony stakeholders mak architectural decisiouns based on the technical interfaces atween the system an its context. Especially infrastructur or hardware designers decide thir technical interfaces. Form E.g. UML deployment diagram describin channels tae neighbourin systems, thegither wi a mappin table shawin the relationships atween channels an input/output. Solution Strategy Summary o the fundamental decisiouns an solution strategies that shape the architectur. Can include technology, tap-level decomposition, approaches tae achieve tap quality goals an relevant organisational decisiouns. Contents A short summary an explanation o the fundamental decisiouns an solution strategies, that shape the system’s architectur. These include technology decisiouns decisiouns aboot the tap-level decomposition o the system, e.g. uisage o an architectural pattern or design pattern decisiouns on hoo tae achieve key quality goals relevant organisational decisiouns, e.g. selectin a development process or delegatin certain tasks tae third pairties. Motivation Thir decisiouns form the cornerstanes for yer architectur. They are the basis for mony ither detailed decisiouns or implementation rules. Form Keep the explanation o thir key decisiouns short. Motivate whit ye hae decidit an why ye decidit that wey, based upon yer problem statement, the quality goals an key constraints. Refer tae details in the follaein sections (section 5 for structural details, section 8 for crosscuttin concepts). Ye micht uise a list o solution-approaches or a table. Biggin Block View Static decomposition o the system, abstractions o source-code, shawn as hierarchy o white boxes (containin black boxes), up tae the appropriate level o detail. Content The biggin block view shaws the static decomposition o the system intae biggin blocks (modules, components, subsystems, classes, interfaces, packages, leebraries, frameworks, layers, partitions, tiers, functions, macros, operatiouns, data structurs, …) as weel as their dependencies (relationships, associatiouns, …) This view is mandatory for ilka architectur documentation. In analogy tae a hoose this is the floor plan. Motivation Keep an owerview o yer source code bi makin its structur unnerstaundable throu abstraction. This lets ye communicate wi yer stakeholder on an abstract level athoot disclosin implementation details. Form The biggin block view is a hierarchial collection o black boxes an white boxes (see figure ablow) an their descriptions. 5.1 Whitebox Owerall System Here ye describe the decomposition o the owerall system uisin the follaein white box template. It contains an owerview diagram a motivation for the decomposition black box descriptions o the containit biggin blocks. For thir we offer ye alternatives: uise ae table for a short an pragmatic owerview o aw containit biggin blocks an their interfaces uise a list o black box descriptions o the biggin blocks accordin tae the black box template (see ablow). Dependin on yer chyce o tuil this list could be sub-chapters (in text files), sub-pages (in a Wiki) or nestit elements (in a modellin tuil). (optional:) important interfaces, that are no explainit in the black box templates o a biggin block, but are unco important for unnerstaunin the white box. Sin there are sae mony weys tae specify interfaces why dae we no provide a specific templat for them. In the best case ye will get awa wi examples or simple signatures. 5.2 Level 2 Here ye can specify the inner structur o (some) biggin blocks frae level 1 as white boxes. Ye hae tae decide which biggin blocks o yer system are important eneuch tae justify sic a detailed description. Please prefer relevance ower completeness. Specify important, surprisin, risky, complex or volatile biggin blocks. Leave oot normal, simple, borin or staundartised pairts o yer system 5.2.1 White Box for biggin block 1 Specifies the internal structur o biggin block 1. Uise the white box templat (see abune). Runtime View Behaviour o biggin blocks as scenarios, coverin important uise cases or features, interactiouns at critical external interfaces, operation an administration plus error an exception behaviour. Content The runtime view describes concrete behaviour an interactiouns o the system’s biggin blocks in form o scenarios frae the follaein areas: important uise cases or features: hoo dae biggin blocks execute them? interactiouns at critical external interfaces: hoo dae biggin blocks cooperate wi uisers an neighbourin systems? operation an administration: launch, start-up, stop error an exception scenarios Remark: The main criterion for the chyce o possible scenarios (sequences, workflows) is their architectural relevancy. It isna important tae describe a muckle nummer o scenarios. Ye sud raither document a representative selection. Motivation Ye sud unnerstaun hoo (instances o) biggin blocks o yer system perform their job an communicate at runtime. Ye will mainly tak doun scenarios in yer documentation tae communicate yer architectur tae stakeholders that are less willin or able tae read an unnerstaun the static models (biggin block view, deployment view). Form There are mony notations for describin scenarios, e.g. numbered list o steps (in natural leid) activity diagrams or flow chairts sequence diagrams BPMN or EPCs (event process chains) state machines etc. 6.n Runtime Scenario n (1, 2, 3, etc.) Insert runtime diagram or textual description o the scenario. Insert description o the notable aspects o the interactiouns atween the biggin block instances depictit in this diagram. Deployment View Technical infrastructur wi environments, computers, processors, topologies. Mappin o (saftware) biggin blocks tae infrastructur elements. Content The deployment view describes: the technical infrastructur uised tae execute yer system, wi infrastructur elements like geographical locatiouns, environments, computers, processors, channels an net topologies as weel as ither infrastructur elements an the mappin o (saftware) biggin blocks tae that infrastructur elements. Aften systems are executit in different environments, e.g. development environment, test environment, production environment. In sic cases ye sud document aw relevant environments. Especially document the deployment view whan yer saftware is executit as distributit system wi mair than ane computer, processor, server or container or whan ye design an construct yer ain hardware processors an chips. Frae a saftware perspective it is sufficient tae tak doun thae elements o the infrastructur that are needit tae shaw the deployment o yer biggin blocks. Hardware architects can gae ayont that an describe the infrastructur tae onie level o detail they need tae tak doun. Motivation Saftware daesna rin athoot hardware. This unnerlyin infrastructur can an will influence yer system and/or some cross-cuttin concepts. Therefore, ye need tae ken the infrastructur. Form Maybe the heichest level deployment diagram is awready containit in section 3.2. as technical context wi yer ain infrastructur as AE black box. In this section ye will zoom intae this black box uisin additional deployment diagrams. UML offers deployment diagrams tae express that view. Uise it, probably wi nestit diagrams, whan yer infrastructur is mair complex. Whan yer (hardware) stakeholders prefer ither kinds o diagrams raither than UML deployment diagram, let them uise onie kind that is able tae shaw nodes an channels o the infrastructur. 7.1 Infrastructur Level 1 Describe (usually in a combination o diagrams, tables, an text): the distribution o yer system tae multiple locatiouns, environments, computers, processors, .. as weel as the physical connectiouns atween them important justification or motivation for this deployment structur quality and/or performance features o the infrastructur the mappin o saftware artefacts (biggin blocks) tae elements o the infrastructur For multiple environments or alternative deployments please copy that section o arc42 for aw relevant environments. 7.2 Infrastructur Level 2 Here ye can include the internal structur o (some) infrastructur elements frae infrastructur level 1. Please copy the structur frae level 1 for each selectit element. Crosscuttin Concepts Owerall, principal regulatiouns an solution approaches relevant in multiple pairts (→ cross-cuttin) o the system. Concepts are aften relatit tae multiple biggin blocks. Include different topics like domain models, architectur patterns an -styles, rules for uisin specific technology an implementation rules. Content This section describes crosscuttin concepts (practices, patterns, regulatiouns or solution ideas). Sic concepts are aften relatit tae multiple biggin blocks. They micht include mony different topics. Motivation Concepts form the basis for conceptual integrity (consistency, homogeneity) o the architectur. Sae, they are an important contribution tae achieve inner qualities o yer system. This is the place in the templat that we providit for a cohesive specification o sic concepts. Mony o thir concepts relate tae or influence several o yer biggin blocks. Form The form can be varied: concept papers wi onie kind o structur example implementatiouns, especially for technical concepts cross-cuttin model excerpts or scenarios uisin notatiouns o the architectur views Structur o this section Pick juist the maist-needit topics for yer system an assign each a level-2 heading in this section (e.g. 8.1, 8.2 etc). DINNAE ATTEMPT tae cover aw o the topics o the aforementioned diagram. Background Some topics within systems aften concern multiple biggin blocks, hardware elements or development processes. It micht be easier tae communicate or document sic cross-cuttin topics at a central locatioun, instead o repeatin them in the description o the concernit biggin blocks, hardware elements or development processes. Certain concepts micht concern aw elements o a system, ithers micht juist be relevant for a few. Architectural Decisions Important, expensive, critical, muckle scale or risky architectur decisiouns includin rationales. Content Important, expensive, muckle scale or risky architectur decisiouns includin rationales. Wi “decisions” we mean selectin ae alternative based on gien criteria. Please uise yer judgement tae decide whether an architectural decisioun sud be documentit here in this central section or whether ye better document it locally (e.g. within the white box templat o ae biggin block). Avoid redundant texts. Refer tae section 4, whaur ye tuik doun the maist important decisiouns o yer architectur awready. Motivation Stakeholders o yer system sud be able tae comprehend an retrace yer decisiouns. Form ADR (architectur decisioun record) for ilka important decisioun list or table, ordered bi importance an consequences or mair detailed in form o separate sections per decisioun Background (on ADRs) Smaller pieces o documentation are easier tae read, mak an keep up. Whan it comes tae architectur decisiouns, development teams will aften: ken aboot the decisioun, as it visible e.g. in source code, but miss the motivation ahint that decisioun (see Nygard 2011) Therefore ye sud document a few important decisiouns thegither wi their motivation, reasonin Oor proposal concernin decisiouns Keep a collection o architecturally significant decisiouns, thae decisiouns that affect the structur, quality characteristics, important (especially external) dependencies an interfaces, or constructioun techniques (thanks tae Michael Nygard for this proposal). Quality Requirements Quality requirements as scenarios, wi quality tree tae provide heich-level owerview. The maist important quality goals sud hae been describit in section 1.2. (quality goals). Content This section contains aw relevant quality requirements. The maist important o thir requirements hae awready been describit in section 1.2. (quality goals), therefore they sud juist be referencit here. In this section 10 ye sud an aw tak doun quality requirements wi lesser importance, which winna mak heich risks whan they arena fully achieved (but micht be nice-tae-hae). Motivation Sin quality requirements will hae a lot o influence on architectural decisiouns ye sud ken whit qualities are really important for yer stakeholders, in a specific an measurable wey. Further Information See the extensive Q42 quality model on https://quality.arc42.org. 10.1 Quality Requirements Owerview Content An owerview or summary o quality requirements. Motivation Aften we come athort dizzens (or even hunders) o detailed quality requirements. In this owerview section ye sud try tae summarise, e.g. bi describin categories or topics (as suggestit bi ISO 25010:2023 or Q42 If thir summary descriptions are awready precise, specific eneuch an measurable, ye micht skip section 10.2. Form Uise a simple table in which each line contains a category or topic an a short description o the quality requirement. Alternatively, ye micht uise a mindmap tae structur thir quality requirements. In literature, the idea o a quality attribute tree haes an aw been describit, which pits the generic term “quality” as the root an uises a tree-like refinement o the term “quality”. [Bass+21] introducit the term “Quality Attribute Utility Tree” for this purpose. 10.2 Quality Scenarios Content Quality scenarios mak quality requirements concrete an allou tae decide whether they are fulfilt (in the sense o acceptance criteria). Ensure that yer scenarios are specific an measurable. Twa kinds o scenarios are especially uiseful: Uisage scenarios (an aw cried application scenarios or uise case scenarios) describe the system’s runtime reaction tae a certain stimulus. This an aw includes scenarios that describe the system’s efficiency or performance. Example: The system reacts tae a uiser’s request within ae second. Chynge scenarios describe the desired effect o a modification or extension o the system or o its immediate environment. Example: Additional functionality is implementit or requirements for a quality attribute chynge, an the effort or duration o the chynge is measured. Form Typical information for detailed scenarios include the follaein: In short form (favoured in the Q42 model): Context/Background: Whit kind o system or component, whit is the environment or situation? Source/Stimulus: Wha or whit initiates or triggers a behaviour, reaction or action. Metric/Acceptance Criteria: A response includin a measure or metric The lang form o scenarios (favoured bi the SEI an [Bass+21]) is mair detailed an includes the follaein information: Scenario ID: A unique identifier for the scenario. Scenario Name: A short, descriptive name for the scenario. Source: The entity (uiser, system, or event) that initiates the scenario. Stimulus: The triggerin event or condition the system maun address. Environment: The operational context or condition unner which the system experiences the stimulus. Artifact: The biggin-blocks or ither elements o the system affectit bi the stimulus. Response: The outcome or behaviour the system exhibits in reaction tae the stimulus. Response Measure: The criteria or metric bi which the system’s response is evaluatit. See also Frae January 2023, arc42 provides a pragmatic quality model, that proposes tae label quality requirements, wi hashtags or labels like #flexible, #efficient, #usable, #operable, #testable, #secure, #safe, #reliable. Risks an Technical Debt Kent technical risks or technical debt. Whit potential problems exist within or roun the system? Whit daes the development team feel meeserable aboot? Content A list o identifiet technical risks or technical debts, ordered bi priority Motivation “Risk management is project management for grown-ups” (Tim Lister, Atlantic Systems Guild.) This sud be yer motto for systematic detection an evaluation o risks an technical debts in the architectur, which will be needit bi management stakeholders (e.g. project managers, product awners) as pairt o the owerall risk analysis an measurement plannin. Form List o risks and/or technical debts, probably includin suggestit measures tae minimise, mitigate or avoid risks or reduce technical debts.

records.text: {Your Title Here} !!! info Status : { Proposed Under Review Accepted Rejected Superseded Deprecated } Updated : {YYYY-MM-DD} Summary {This is the 'executive summary' or 'elevator pitch' for yer ADR. In a few concise sentences (typically 2-4), clearly state the core problem, question, or opportunity this ADR addresses. Include a brief hint at the decisioun made or the area o focus. The aim is tae help readers quickly unnerstaun whit this ADR is aboot an decide if it's relevant tae them, athoot needin tae read the haill document. Think o it as the abstract o a technical paper or a unco brief introduction tae the main topic.} Drivers {This section explains why this decisioun is bein made noo . Clearly articulate the primary motivations, needs, or problems that necessitate this architectural decisioun. Think aboot the unnerlyin reasons an pressures.} {e.g. We are developin a new feature/capability that needs...} {e.g. We need to improve performance, accessibility, remove debt...} {e.g. Feedback from users suggests...} {e.g. The current approach imposes these limitations...} Options {This is whaur ye list the different options ye are considerin. Stick tae the facts an avoid opinions, the neist section covers the analysis. Include a concise description, links tae relevant documentation or examples. Include aw significant alternatives ye explored, even if they werena finally chosen. The aim is tae gie readers a clear, unbiased unnerstaunin o each alternative afore ye dive intae the evaluation.} {Option 1 Title} {Describe the option, provide a summary, list the facts, provide links etc.} {Option n Title} ... Options Analysis {This is whaur ye critically evaluate each option presentit in the Options section. For each option, provide a balanced view o its advantages, disadvantages, an onie ither relevant considerations or trade-offs. Be specific an, whaur possible, relate yer pynts back tae the Drivers . Consider aspects like: Cost (development, operational, licensing) Complexity (implementation, maintenance, learning curve) Risks (technical, operational, security) Alignment wi architectural principles or existin staundarts Impact on performance, scalability, usability, maintainability, security, etc. Include as mony Pro/Con/Other statements as required. } {Option 1 Assessment} Pro: {A specific advantage or benefit o this option.} Con: {A specific disadvantage, risk, or cost associatit wi this option.} Other: {A relevant pynt that isna strictly a pro or con.} {Option n Assessment} ... Recommendation {This is whaur ye clearly state the final decisioun, an explicitly name the option that haes been selectit. Explain in detail why this option wis chosen. Ye sud clearly articulate hoo the chosen option best addresses the Drivers an meets the key requirements or solves the statit problem.} Consequences {This section is optional .} {Noo that a decisioun haes been made whit are the expectit outcomes an impacts, baith positive an negative? Whit kent limitatiouns, costs, or risks are bein acceptit bi makin this decisioun? Hoo will this decisioun affect different stakeholders, ither systems, development practices, operational procedures, or user experience?} Pro: {A specific positive outcome or benefit expectit frae this decisioun.} Con: {A specific acceptit downside, cost, or risk resultin frae this decisioun. } Other: {A consequence that isna strictly a pro or con.} Confirmation {This section is optional .} {Outline hoo the implementation o this decisioun will be verifiet an hoo ongoin compliance will be ensured. This helps demonstrate that the decisioun isna juist theoretical but will be actively pit intae practice an monitored. Hoo will ye check that the decisioun haes been correctly implementit? (e.g., code reviews, specific tests, demonstrations, peer review). Hoo will adherence tae this decisioun be keepit up ower time? (e.g., automatit checks, periodic audits, updates tae team guidelines, trainin). Are there specific metrics or indicators that will shaw the decisioun is achievin its intendit positive outcomes? (e.g., performance benchmarks, adoption rates, reduction in specific errors, user feedback scores). Wha is responsible for oversein this, an whit happens if the decisioun isna follaed?} More Information {This section is optional .} {Uise this section tae provide onie supplementary information that supports the decisioun, adds context, or guides future actions. Links tae ither decisiouns an resources micht appear here an aw. Ye could briefly note wha wis involved in the decisioun-makin process an if/hoo consensus wis reached. Ye micht an aw want tae suggest a timeframe or specific events that micht prompt a re-evaluation o this decisioun in the future.}

headings: Decisioun record templat bi Jeff Tyree an Art Akerman
records.text: Decisioun record templat bi Jeff Tyree an Art Akerman This is the architectur decisioun description templat publisht in "Architecture Decisions: Demystifying Architecture" by Jeff Tyree and Art Akerman, Capital One Financial. Issue : Describe the architectural design issue ye're addressin, leavin nae questions aboot why ye're addressin this issue noo. Follaein a minimalist approach, address an document juist the issues that need addressin at various pynts in the life cycle. Decision : Clearly state the architectur’s direction—that is, the position ye’ve selectit. Status : The decisioun’s status, sic as pendin, decidit, or approved. Group : Ye can uise a simple groupin—sic as integration, presentation, data, an sae on—tae help organise the set o decisiouns. Ye could an aw uise a mair sophisticatit architectur ontology, sic as John Kyaruzi an Jan van Katwijk’s, which includes mair abstract categories sic as event, calendar, an location. For example, uisin this ontology, ye’d group decisiouns that deal wi occurrences whaur the system requires information unner event. Assumptions : Clearly describe the unnerlyin assumptiouns in the environment in which ye’re makin the decisioun—cost, schedule, technology, an sae on. Note that environmental constraints (sic as acceptit technology staundarts, enterprise architectur, commonly employit patterns, an sae on) micht limit the alternatives ye consider. Constraints : Tak doun onie additional constraints tae the environment that the chosen alternative (the decisioun) micht pose. Positions : List the positiouns (viable options or alternatives) ye consideret. These aften require lang explanatiouns, whiles even models an diagrams. This isna an exhaustive list. But, ye dinnae want tae hear the question "Did you think about...?" durin a final review; this leads tae loss o credibility an questionin o ither architectural decisiouns. This section an aw helps ensure that ye heard ithers’ opinions; explicitly statin ither opinions helps enrol their advocates in yer decisioun. Argument : Outline why ye selectit a position, includin items sic as implementation cost, total ownership cost, time tae market, an the availability o required development resources. This is probably as important as the decisioun itsel. Implications : A decisioun comes wi mony implicatiouns, as the REMAP metamodel denotes. For example, a decisioun micht introduce a need tae mak ither decisiouns, mak new requirements, or modify existin requirements; pose additional constraints tae the environment; require renegotiatin scope or schedule wi customers; or require additional staff trainin. Clearly unnerstaunin an statin yer decisioun’s implicatiouns can be unco effective in gaein buy-in an makin a roadmap for architectur execution. Related decisions : It’s obvious that mony decisiouns are relatit; ye can list them here. But, we’ve found that in practice, a traceability matrix, decisioun trees, or metamodels are mair uiseful. Metamodels are uiseful for shawin complex relationships diagrammatically (sic as Rose models). Related requirements : Decisiouns sud be business driven. Tae shaw accountability, explicitly map yer decisiouns tae the objectives or requirements. Ye can enumerate thir relatit requirements here, but we’ve found it mair convenient tae reference a traceability matrix. Ye can assess each architectur decisioun’s contribution tae meetin each requirement, an than assess hoo weel the requirement is met athort aw decisiouns. If a decisioun doesna contribute tae meetin a requirement, dinnae mak that decisioun. Related artifacts : List the relatit architectur, design, or scope documents that this decisioun impacts. Related principles : If the enterprise haes an agreed-upon set o principles, mak siccar the decisioun is consistent wi ane or mair o them. This helps ensure alignment alang domains or systems. Notes : Acause the decisioun-makin process can tak weeks, we’ve found it uiseful tae tak doun notes an issues that the team discusses durin the socialisation process.

ITDs are a focused evolution o ADRs, optimised for speed, clarity, an executive validation. Whaur an ADR documents whit wis decidit, an ITD is a lean, decisioun-first artefact that maks the decisioun itsel reviewable, sae stakeholders can scan it quickly an challenge it easily. ITDs are weel suitit tae technical decisiouns that are no strictly architectural, sic as chuisin a model, a leebrary, or a CI/CD strategy. In each ITD file, scrieve thir sections: Title State the decisioun itsel, no a description o the topic. For example, "Use Qwen2.5 1.5B Instruct for on-device translation". The Problem Ae sentence statin whit we are tryin tae solve. Options Considered The alternatives that were on the table, wi the selectit option in bold . Rationale Juist the decisive factors that led tae the chyce, no an exhaustive list o ilka pro an con. Notes Optional.
